questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India states that the Parliament consists of the President of India and the two Houses of Parliament known as Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and House of the People (Lok Sabha)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 79**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 79** of the Constitution of India states that the Parliament consists of the President of India and the two Houses of Parliament, namely the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
 
• The President of India is an integral part of the Parliament, although not a member of either House.
 
• The Parliament operates as a bicameral legislature with **Rajya Sabha representing the states and union territories** and **Lok Sabha representing the citizens** through direct elections.
 
• This article is a fundamental provision under **Part V (The Union) and Chapter II (Parliament)** of the Constitution of India.
 
• Article 79 establishes the structure and functioning of the Parliament, ensuring a collaborative legislative process between the President and the two Houses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajya Sabha (Council of States)**

 
 
• Rajya Sabha is the upper house of Parliament, representing the states and union territories of India.
 
• It is a **permanent body** that is not subject to dissolution, with one-third of its members retiring every two years.
 
• The **maximum strength** of Rajya Sabha is capped at 250 members as per Article 80 of the Constitution.
 
• The Vice President of India acts as the **ex-officio Chairman** of Rajya Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Lok Sabha (House of the People)**
 
 
• Lok Sabha is the lower house of Parliament, with members directly elected by the citizens of India.
 
• The maximum strength of Lok Sabha is **552 members**, including up to 20 members representing Union Territories.
 
• The Speaker of Lok Sabha presides over its sessions and ensures the orderly conduct of business.
 
• It serves as the principal legislative body for **enacting laws** and addressing the needs of the electorate.
 
 
 
• **Role of the President in Parliament**
 
 
• The President summons and prorogues sessions of Parliament and grants assent to bills to convert them into laws.
 
• The President can **dissolve Lok Sabha** and call for fresh elections when necessary.
 
• Under Article 123, the President can issue ordinances when Parliament is not in session.
 
• The President is a crucial part of the legislative process but does not vote or participate in debates.
 
 
 
• **Bicameral Legislature System**
 
 
• India follows a bicameral legislature, consisting of two houses: Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha.
 
• The system ensures **checks and balances** in the legislative process, preventing hasty decisions.
 
• Rajya Sabha focuses on states and union territories, while Lok Sabha represents citizens directly.
 
• Countries like the USA, UK, and Canada also follow bicameral legislature systems.

questions.question: Which edition of the Santosh Trophy event did Karnataka win in the 2022-23 season?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**76th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Karnataka won the **76th edition** of the Santosh Trophy during the 2022-23 season.
 
• The final match was held on **March 4, 2023**, where Karnataka defeated Meghalaya with a score of **3-2**.
 
• This victory marked Karnataka's **first Santosh Trophy win in 54 years**, with their last win dating back to the 1968-69 season.
 
• The tournament was hosted in **Saudi Arabia** for the first time, as part of the All India Football Federation's initiative to globalize Indian football.
 
• The Santosh Trophy is an annual football competition in India contested by **state teams and government institutions**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Santosh Trophy**

 
 
• Named after Maharaja Sir Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhary of Santosh, a key patron of Indian football.
 
• Established in **1941**, the tournament is organized by the **All India Football Federation (AIFF)**.
 
• The competition primarily features teams from Indian states, Union Territories, and government institutions.
 
• It serves as a platform for grassroots-level football development and talent identification in India.
 
 
 
• **Karnataka's Football Legacy**
 
 
• Karnataka, formerly known as Mysore, has a rich footballing history, with its last Santosh Trophy win occurring in the **1968-69 season**.
 
• Notable footballers, including **Sunil Chhetri**, hail from Karnataka, contributing to Indian football's growth.
 
• Clubs like **Bengaluru FC** have further cemented the state's reputation as a football hub.
 
 
 
• **AIFF Initiatives**
 
 
• The All India Football Federation (AIFF) aims to globalize Indian football through international collaborations and tournaments.
 
• Hosting the Santosh Trophy in Saudi Arabia provided a platform to showcase Indian football on a global stage.
 
• Other initiatives, such as the **Indian Super League (ISL)** and youth development programs, aim to strengthen football infrastructure in India.
 
 
 
• **Meghalaya's Performance**
 
 
• Meghalaya reached the Santosh Trophy final for the **first time** in the 2022-23 season.
 
• Their performance highlighted the growing football culture and talent in **Northeastern India**.
 
• Despite their loss, Meghalaya's journey to the final was widely praised and is expected to inspire further football development in the region.

questions.question: Ortho-sulphobenzimide is one of the artificial sweeteners. It is also known as _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Saccharin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Saccharin, also known as Ortho-sulphobenzimide, is one of the oldest artificial sweeteners and a popular sugar substitute.
 
• It is approximately 300–400 times sweeter than sucrose (table sugar), requiring only a small amount to achieve desired sweetness.
 
• Saccharin is calorie-free, making it suitable for people managing weight or controlling diabetes.
 
• It is widely used in products such as diet beverages, baked goods, toothpaste, and pharmaceutical formulations due to its stability under heat and storage.
 
• Saccharin was discovered in 1879 by Constantin Fahlberg and became commercially available in the early 20th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Artificial Sweeteners:**

 
 
• Artificial sweeteners are chemical compounds that mimic the sweetness of sugar while providing fewer or no calories.
 
• Examples include saccharin, aspartame, sucralose, and alitame, which are widely used in food and beverages.
 
• They are commonly used to aid in calorie reduction and diabetes management.
 
 
 
• **Aspartame:**
 
 
• Aspartame is an artificial sweetener that is about 200 times sweeter than sucrose.
 
• It is commonly found in diet sodas, sugar-free gum, and other low-calorie products.
 
• Unlike saccharin, aspartame provides calories but is used in very small amounts, making its caloric contribution negligible.
 
 
 
• **Sucralose:**
 
 
• Sucralose is a chlorinated derivative of sucrose and is about 600 times sweeter than regular sugar.
 
• It is heat-stable and is commonly used in baking and cooking.
 
• Sucralose is marketed under the brand name Splenda.
 
 
 
• **Health Considerations:**
 
 
• Artificial sweeteners like saccharin are approved by regulatory authorities for safe consumption.
 
• Saccharin was once linked to cancer in laboratory animals, but subsequent studies confirmed its safety for humans within regulated limits.
 
• Regulatory bodies like the FDA and WHO continuously monitor the safety of artificial sweeteners.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an iron-ore producing belt of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bilaspur-Panipat belt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bilaspur-Panipat belt is **NOT an iron-ore producing region** in India.
 
• India’s major iron-ore producing belts are the **Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt**, **Odisha-Jharkhand belt**, and **Maharashtra-Goa belt**.
 
• The **Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt** in Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra is known for its high-grade hematite ores, with major mines like Bailadila.
 
• The **Odisha-Jharkhand belt** includes key mines such as Barbil, Noamundi, and Gua, contributing significantly to India’s total iron ore output.
 
• The **Maharashtra-Goa belt** is famous for low-grade iron ore, with Goa playing a significant role in exports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron Ore in India:**

 
 
• Iron ore is a key raw material for steel production, with India being one of the largest producers globally.
 
• Major types of iron ore found in India include **hematite** (high-grade, widely used) and **magnetite** (low-grade).
 
 
 
• **Bailadila Mines:**
 
 
• Located in the Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt in Chhattisgarh.
 
• They produce some of the highest-grade hematite ore in India, which is used domestically and exported.
 
 
 
• **Odisha-Jharkhand Belt:**
 
 
• Odisha is India’s largest producer of iron ore, contributing around **50%** of the country’s total production.
 
• Keonjhar and Sundargarh districts are prominent mining regions.
 
 
 
• **Goa’s Contribution to Iron Ore:**
 
 
• Known for low-grade iron ore, which is primarily exported to countries like China and Japan.
 
• Mining activities in Goa have faced regulatory challenges in recent years.

questions.question: Which of the following was the capital of the Pallava Dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kanchipuram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kanchipuram** served as the capital of the Pallava Dynasty, which ruled parts of South India from the 3rd to 9th centuries CE.
 
• The Pallavas are renowned for their contributions to **Dravidian art and architecture**, and Kanchipuram became a prominent center for temple architecture under their reign.
 
• The city is home to notable structures such as the **Kailasanatha Temple** and **Vaikunta Perumal Temple**, exemplifying the architectural advancements during the Pallava era.
 
• Kanchipuram was also an important center for **learning and spirituality**, fostering both Hinduism and Buddhism during the Pallava period.
 
• The Pallavas played a key role in spreading Indian art, architecture, and culture to Southeast Asia through trade and cultural exchanges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pallava Dynasty**

 
 
• The Pallavas were a powerful South Indian dynasty that ruled over Tamil Nadu and parts of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• They were contemporaries of other prominent dynasties like the Chalukyas and Pandyas.
 
• Their reign marked the transition from **rock-cut architecture to structural temples**, influencing later dynasties such as the Cholas.
 
• They were patrons of both **Sanskrit and Tamil literature**, contributing significantly to the cultural and intellectual heritage of South India.
 
 
 
• **Kanchipuram**
 
 
• Known as the **"City of Thousand Temples"**, Kanchipuram is one of the seven sacred cities of Hinduism.
 
• It served as a major political, economic, and spiritual hub during the Pallava period.
 
• The city is famous for **Kanchipuram silk sarees**, which are a significant cultural legacy.
 
• It has been a center for various religious traditions, including Shaivism, Vaishnavism, and Jainism.
 
 
 
• **Pallava Architecture**
 
 
• The Pallavas pioneered **rock-cut architecture**, evident in the Mahabalipuram cave temples.
 
• Later, they transitioned to structural temples made of stone, such as the **Kailasanatha Temple** in Kanchipuram.
 
• The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram, built during Pallava rule, is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
 
• Their architectural innovations set the foundation for Dravidian temple architecture in South India.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance**
 
 
• The Pallavas were instrumental in spreading Indian culture and religion to Southeast Asia through maritime trade and cultural exchanges.
 
• Their inscriptions, written in both Tamil and Sanskrit, provide valuable insights into the political and cultural history of ancient South India.
 
• Their governance and cultural achievements laid the groundwork for subsequent South Indian dynasties, such as the Cholas.
 
• Their advancements in art and architecture had a lasting impact on the cultural landscape of India and beyond.

questions.question: Hareli festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hareli is a traditional agricultural festival celebrated primarily in the state of **Chhattisgarh, India**.
 
• The festival is observed in the Hindu month of **Shravan (July-August)** and marks the beginning of the agricultural season.
 
• Farmers worship farm tools, bullocks, and plows, and offer prayers to deities such as **Goddess Hareli** and **Mother Earth**.
 
• The celebrations include decorating bullocks, preparing traditional dishes, and engaging in unique local games like **Gedi (walking on bamboo stilts)**.
 
• The festival symbolizes gratitude to nature and prayers for a **good harvest, prosperity, and the well-being** of families and livestock.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agricultural Festivals in India**

 
 
• India celebrates various agriculture-related festivals reflecting its farming culture, such as **Pongal (Tamil Nadu)**, **Baisakhi (Punjab)**, **Onam (Kerala)**, and **Makar Sankranti** (across India).
 
• These festivals often signify seasonal changes and the **harvesting of crops**, emphasizing the agrarian lifestyle of the country.
 
• They promote community bonding and **preserve indigenous traditions**.
 
 
 
• **Chhattisgarh's Cultural Heritage**
 
 
• Chhattisgarh is known as the **"Rice Bowl of India"** due to its vast paddy fields and rich agricultural practices.
 
• The state has a vibrant tribal culture, highlighted through festivals like **Bastar Dussehra**, **Madai**, and Hareli.
 
• These festivals represent **Chhattisgarh's unique cultural identity** and traditions.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Livestock in Farming**
 
 
• Livestock is crucial in traditional farming, providing **draught power, manure, and additional income** through dairy products.
 
• Festivals like Hareli emphasize the role of livestock by incorporating rituals to honor and care for animals.
 
• This practice aligns with sustainable farming techniques by integrating **animal husbandry** into agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Connection Between Festivals and Sustainability**
 
 
• Agricultural festivals like Hareli foster a deeper connection between humans and nature.
 
• They promote **sustainable farming practices** and respect for natural resources.
 
• Such celebrations encourage the sharing of **traditional knowledge** among farming communities.

questions.question: Kamalini Asthana is associated with which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kamalini Asthana** is a renowned exponent of the classical Indian dance form Kathak.
 
• Kathak is one of the eight recognized classical dance forms of India, known for its intricate footwork, spins, and storytelling through expressions.
 
• The dance form originated in northern India and evolved from temple performances narrating stories from Hindu epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana.
 
• Kamalini Asthana has significantly contributed to preserving and promoting Kathak globally, furthering its cultural heritage.
 
• Kathak incorporates rhythmic compositions such as "tihai" (a phrase repeated thrice), graceful gestures (mudras), and the use of ankle bells (ghungroos) to create intricate patterns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Classical Dance Forms of India**

 
 
• India has eight classical dance forms recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Odissi, and Sattriya.
 
• These dance forms are rooted in the Natya Shastra, an ancient Sanskrit text on performing arts authored by Bharata.
 
• Each form represents unique cultural and regional traditions of India.
 
 
 
• **Kathak Gharanas**
 
 
• Kathak has three prominent gharanas (schools): Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras.
 
• The Lucknow Gharana emphasizes grace and expressions, the Jaipur Gharana focuses on vigorous footwork, and the Banaras Gharana highlights devotional themes.
 
 
 
• **Key Elements of Kathak**
 
 
• Kathak includes "Nritta" (pure dance), "Nritya" (expressive dance), and "Natya" (dramatic storytelling).
 
• The use of ghungroos (ankle bells) is essential to enhance the rhythmic quality of Kathak performances.
 
• The dance often incorporates complex rhythmic cycles (tala) and improvisations by the performer.
 
 
 
• **Notable Kathak Artists**
 
 
• Legendary artists such as Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi, and Kamalini Asthana have played pivotal roles in popularizing Kathak globally.
 
• These artists have preserved traditional Kathak while adapting it to modern platforms, ensuring its continued relevance.

questions.question: ICC Women's T-20 Cricket World Cup is a/an ________ event.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ICC Women's T-20 Cricket World Cup is a biennial event**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The ICC Women's T-20 Cricket World Cup is held every two years, making it a **biennial event**.
 
• The tournament is governed by the **International Cricket Council (ICC)** and features top women's cricket teams from across the globe.
 
• The inaugural edition of the ICC Women's T20 World Cup was held in **2009 in England**.
 
• Australia is the most successful team in the tournament's history, winning **six titles as of 2023**.
 
• The competition follows the T20 format, with **20 overs per side**, offering a fast-paced and action-packed cricketing experience.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ICC Women's Cricket World Cup**

 
 
• This is a separate tournament from the T20 World Cup and follows a **One-Day International (ODI) format**.
 
• It is held every **four years** and features 50-over matches.
 
• The first Women's Cricket World Cup was held in **1973 in England**, two years before the men's version.
 
• Australia also dominates the Women's ODI World Cup, with the most titles in its history.
 
 
 
• **T20 Cricket Format**
 
 
• T20 cricket consists of a maximum of **20 overs per team**, making it shorter and more dynamic than other formats.
 
• This format was introduced to attract a wider and younger audience to cricket.
 
• Matches are typically completed in approximately **three hours**, making it suitable for modern sports entertainment.
 
• T20 cricket emphasizes **aggressive batting, innovative bowling, and dynamic fielding**.
 
 
 
• **International Cricket Council (ICC)**
 
 
• The ICC is the governing body of international cricket, founded in **1909** as the Imperial Cricket Conference.
 
• It is headquartered in **Dubai, UAE**, and oversees all major international cricket tournaments.
 
• The ICC aims to grow the sport globally, promoting inclusivity and gender equality.
 
 
 
• **Women's Cricket Development**
 
 
• Women's cricket has grown significantly in popularity and professionalism in recent years.
 
• Leagues like the **Women's Big Bash League** in Australia and **The Hundred** in England have contributed to its development.
 
• Increased media coverage and sponsorship have boosted visibility and financial support for women's cricket.
 
• Initiatives like the ICC Women's T20 World Cup have provided a platform for showcasing women's talent at an international level.

questions.question: The founders of Vijayanagar empire, Harihara and Bukka Raya were the ministers of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kampili**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The founders of the Vijayanagar Empire, Harihara and Bukka Raya, were originally ministers in the kingdom of **Kampili**.
 
• Kampili was a small but strategically significant kingdom located in present-day Karnataka.
 
• The kingdom of Kampili resisted invasions by the Delhi Sultanate under Muhammad bin Tughlaq in the early 14th century.
 
• After the fall of Kampili to the Delhi Sultanate, Harihara and Bukka were captured and reportedly converted to Islam but later reconverted to Hinduism by the sage Vidyaranya.
 
• Inspired by Vidyaranya, Harihara and Bukka went on to establish the Vijayanagar Empire in 1336 CE on the banks of the Tungabhadra River.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kampili Kingdom:**

 
 
• Kampili was ruled by King Kampiladeva, who resisted the Delhi Sultanate's invasions with great valor but was eventually defeated.
 
• The kingdom's fall marked a turning point in South Indian history, leading to the rise of the Vijayanagar Empire.
 
 
 
• **Vidyaranya:**
 
 
• Vidyaranya was a prominent Hindu saint and scholar who played a crucial role in the establishment of the Vijayanagar Empire.
 
• He served as the spiritual advisor to Harihara and Bukka and worked to revive Hindu culture in South India.
 
 
 
• **Vijayanagar Empire:**
 
 
• Founded in 1336 CE by Harihara and Bukka, the Vijayanagar Empire became one of the most powerful South Indian empires.
 
• The empire was known for its advancements in art, architecture, and administration, with Hampi as its capital.
 
• It reached its zenith during the reign of Krishnadevaraya (1509–1529 CE).
 
 
 
• **Battle of Talikota:**
 
 
• The Vijayanagar Empire fell after its defeat in the Battle of Talikota in 1565 CE against the combined forces of the Deccan Sultanates.
 
• Despite its fall, the empire's cultural and historical legacy continues to influence South India.

questions.question: In May 2023, which Chief Minister was honoured with the Bharat Ratna Dr. Ambedkar award for creating a fear-free state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yogi Adityanath**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Yogi Adityanath**, the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, was honored with the Bharat Ratna Dr. Ambedkar Award in May 2023.
 
• The award was given in recognition of his efforts to create a **fear-free state** through effective governance and law enforcement.
 
• Yogi Adityanath's administration has focused on **enhancing law and order**, reducing crime rates, and ensuring public safety in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• His government introduced several initiatives aimed at the **empowerment of women** and marginalized communities, contributing to societal upliftment.
 
• The Bharat Ratna Dr. Ambedkar Award is a prestigious recognition for contributions toward **social justice**, governance, and the principles advocated by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**

 
 
• Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar was a renowned jurist, economist, social reformer, and the **architect of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• He championed the cause of **social justice, equality, and the upliftment of marginalized communities** in India.
 
• Ambedkar's principles continue to inspire awards and initiatives promoting governance aligned with his vision.
 
 
 
• **Law and Order in Uttar Pradesh**
 
 
• Under Yogi Adityanath's leadership, Uttar Pradesh witnessed **improved law enforcement** measures, reducing organized crime and enhancing public safety.
 
• Initiatives like the **Anti-Romeo Squad** targeted crimes against women, ensuring their safety in public spaces.
 
• Technological reforms, such as **e-FIRs and digitization of police records**, have improved transparency and efficiency in governance.
 
 
 
• **Bharat Ratna Dr. Ambedkar Award**
 
 
• This award honors individuals or organizations that contribute significantly to **social justice and governance**, reflecting Dr. Ambedkar's principles.
 
• Recipients are recognized for their work in improving societal conditions and implementing inclusive governance models.
 
 
 
• **Governance Principles of Yogi Adityanath**
 
 
• Yogi Adityanath's governance emphasizes **transparency, accountability, and public service delivery**.
 
• His administration focuses on **infrastructure development, healthcare, and education reforms** to benefit citizens.
 
• Efforts to empower marginalized communities and ensure public safety have been central to his leadership.

questions.question: Identify the group of states that is a part of Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (As of June 2022).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (GKRA) was launched by the Government of India on **20 June 2020** to address the economic challenges faced by migrant workers returning home during the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• The scheme focuses on creating livelihood opportunities and developing durable rural infrastructure in **116 districts across six states**, including Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand.
 
• Along with Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand, the other participating states are Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, and Rajasthan.
 
• The initiative aligns with the government's objective to provide employment through **25 categories of public works**, such as rural housing, sanitation, road construction, and water conservation.
 
• The scheme was allocated an initial funding of **₹50,000 crore** to create immediate employment opportunities and support rural development in affected regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Objective of GKRA:**

 
 
• The primary aim is to provide immediate employment to migrant workers and create durable rural infrastructure.
 
• The scheme integrates existing government programs such as MGNREGA, PMGSY, and Jal Jeevan Mission to expedite development.
 
 
 
• **Targeted Districts:**
 
 
• The 116 districts were selected based on data showing high concentrations of returning migrant workers.
 
• These districts span across six states, including Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand.
 
 
 
• **Implementation:**
 
 
• The Ministry of Rural Development spearheads the program with support from 12 other central ministries.
 
• Local panchayats were involved in mapping returning workers to ensure efficient targeting of benefits.
 
 
 
• **Skill Development:**
 
 
• GKRA focuses on skill development for workers to enhance their employability in the long term.
 
• The scheme seeks to build capacities in areas like construction, agriculture, and allied sectors.
 
 
 
• **COVID-19 Context:**
 
 
• The pandemic caused a massive reverse migration of workers from urban to rural areas, necessitating immediate livelihood interventions.
 
• GKRA served as a critical measure to mitigate the socioeconomic impact of the pandemic in rural India.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements with reference to Padma Subrahmanyam is/are correct?

1) Padma Subrahmanyam is a famous Bharatanatyam dancer.

2) She received the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan awards.

3) She was also honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Dance.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1, 2, and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Padma Subrahmanyam is a globally renowned Bharatanatyam dancer, celebrated for her innovative contributions to Indian classical dance.
 
• She received the Padma Shri award in 1981 and the Padma Bhushan award in 2003, acknowledging her exceptional contributions to Indian art and culture.
 
• She was honoured with the prestigious Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Dance in 1983, India's highest award for performing arts.
 
• Padma Subrahmanyam is known for her extensive research on Natya Shastra, the ancient Indian treatise on performing arts, and reviving its 108 Karanas (dance movements).
 
• Her choreographic works are lauded for seamlessly integrating traditional Bharatanatyam with innovative interpretations based on her research.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam**

 
 
• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating in Tamil Nadu, and is deeply rooted in temple traditions.
 
• It is characterized by intricate footwork, graceful expressions, and elaborate hand gestures (mudras) that narrate spiritual themes and stories.
 
• The dance is often accompanied by Carnatic music and uses rhythmic patterns to synchronize movements with beats.
 
• The traditional Bharatanatyam costume and jewelry reflect South Indian heritage and temple art.
 
 
 
• **Natya Shastra**
 
 
• Natya Shastra, attributed to sage Bharata, is an ancient Indian treatise on performing arts, including dance, music, and drama.
 
• It serves as the foundational text for Indian classical dance forms, including Bharatanatyam.
 
• The text describes the 108 Karanas (dance movements), which form a significant part of the Bharatanatyam repertoire.
 
• Padma Subrahmanyam's research and revival of the Karanas have significantly contributed to the understanding and practice of classical dance.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi**
 
 
• Established in 1952, Sangeet Natak Akademi is India's national academy for music, dance, and drama.
 
• It functions under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, to promote and preserve India's performing arts heritage.
 
• The Akademi Awards are the highest recognition given to artists for outstanding contributions to their respective fields of performing arts.
 
 
 
• **Padma Awards**
 
 
• Instituted in 1954, the Padma Awards are among India's highest civilian honours.
 
• They are conferred in three categories: Padma Shri (distinguished service), Padma Bhushan (distinguished service of higher order), and Padma Vibhushan (exceptional and distinguished service).
 
• The awards are presented by the President of India at ceremonial functions held at Rashtrapati Bhavan.
 
• Padma Subrahmanyam's recognition with the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan awards highlights her enduring legacy in Indian classical dance.

questions.question: Which of the following is an autobiography of Abul Kalam Azad, the first education minister of India?

options.text: The Story of My Experiments with Truth

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **India Wins Freedom** is the autobiography of Abul Kalam Azad, the first Education Minister of independent India.
 
• The book offers a detailed account of India's struggle for independence and Azad's role as a leader of the Indian National Congress.
 
• It provides insights into key political and social developments, including the partition of India and the challenges faced during nation-building.
 
• Abul Kalam Azad was a staunch advocate of Hindu-Muslim unity and played a significant role in shaping modern India's education policy.
 
• The autobiography was published posthumously in 1959 and remains a crucial source for understanding India's independence movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Abul Kalam Azad**

 
 
• Born on November 11, 1888, in Mecca, Azad was a freedom fighter, scholar, and senior leader of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He became the first Minister of Education in independent India and emphasized universal primary education and education for women.
 
• In his honor, November 11 is celebrated as National Education Day in India.
 
 
 
• **Contributions to Education**
 
 
• Azad helped establish institutions like IITs, the University Grants Commission (UGC), and the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR).
 
• He laid the foundation for Sahitya Akademi and promoted cultural and educational advancements in India.
 
 
 
• **Other Related Works**
 
 
• **The Story of My Experiments with Truth:** Autobiography of Mahatma Gandhi, focusing on his life philosophy and political journey.
 
• **My Country My Life:** Autobiography of L.K. Advani, documenting his political career and contributions to the BJP.
 
• **Long Walk to Freedom:** Autobiography of Nelson Mandela, chronicling his fight against apartheid in South Africa.
 
 
 
• **India Wins Freedom**
 
 
• The book provides a personal perspective on India’s freedom struggle, including Azad's views on the partition and its impact.
 
• It is considered an essential resource for understanding the political dynamics of pre-independence India.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula for potassium permanganate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**KMnO₄**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Potassium permanganate has the chemical formula **KMnO₄**, consisting of potassium (K), manganese (Mn), and oxygen (O).
 
• It is a dark purple crystalline compound widely used as a **strong oxidizing agent** in chemical reactions.
 
• KMnO₄ readily dissolves in water to form potassium ions (K⁺) and permanganate ions (MnO₄−).
 
• The manganese in KMnO₄ has an oxidation state of **+7**, which contributes to its oxidizing properties.
 
• Potassium permanganate is used in **water treatment, disinfection, and various oxidation reactions in organic and inorganic chemistry.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxidizing Properties of KMnO₄:**

 
 
• In acidic conditions, KMnO₄ reduces to Mn²⁺, releasing oxygen and acting as a strong oxidizer.
 
• In neutral or alkaline mediums, it reduces to MnO₂ (manganese dioxide).
 
• Its oxidizing ability is useful in redox titrations and industrial applications.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Potassium Permanganate:**
 
 
• It is used for **purifying and disinfecting water** by oxidizing organic impurities and iron or manganese in water.
 
• Medicinally, it is employed as an antiseptic for treating skin conditions like fungal infections and wounds.
 
• In organic chemistry, KMnO₄ is used to oxidize alkenes to glycols and alcohols to carboxylic acids.
 
 
 
• **Structure of Permanganate Ion:**
 
 
• The permanganate ion (MnO₄−) has a tetrahedral geometry.
 
• Manganese is surrounded by four oxygen atoms, with double-bond character distributed via resonance.
 
 
 
• **Safety Considerations:**
 
 
• KMnO₄ is a strong oxidizer and can ignite combustible materials upon contact.
 
• Direct contact can cause skin irritation and permanent stains, while ingestion is toxic and harmful.
 
• It should be stored in a cool, dry place, away from organic materials to prevent decomposition.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about pteridophytes are correct?

Statements:

A. They include horsetails and ferns.

B. Pteridophytes are used for medicinal purposes and as soil-binders.

C. They are very advanced type of plants on earth, which evolved very recently.

D. Evolutionarily, they are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues – xylem and phloem.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only A, B and D**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pteridophytes** include horsetails and ferns, which are vascular plants widely distributed in terrestrial ecosystems. (Source: NCERT Biology Textbook, Class 11)
 
• Pteridophytes serve ecological and economic purposes, such as being used for medicinal applications and acting as soil-binders to prevent erosion. (Source: Current Environmental Science Research)
 
• Evolutionarily, pteridophytes are the **first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues** like xylem and phloem for water and nutrient transportation. (Source: NCERT Biology Textbook, Class 11)
 
• Pteridophytes are ancient plants that bridge the gap between bryophytes and gymnosperms; they are not recently evolved or highly advanced plants. (Source: Evolutionary Botany Studies)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vascular Tissues in Plants:**

 
 
• Xylem primarily carries water and dissolved minerals, while phloem transports organic nutrients like sugars.
 
• The presence of vascular tissues marks the evolutionary advancement of pteridophytes compared to bryophytes.
 
 
 
• **Horsetails and Ferns:**
 
 
• Horsetails belong to the genus *Equisetum* and are characterized by jointed stems and spore-based reproduction.
 
• Ferns are non-flowering vascular plants with large, divided leaves known as fronds.
 
• Both horsetails and ferns are widely used in horticulture and ecological restoration projects.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Role of Pteridophytes:**
 
 
• Pteridophytes contribute to soil stabilization, especially in areas prone to erosion.
 
• They play an important role in the carbon cycle by sequestering carbon dioxide through photosynthesis.
 
• Several species are utilized for ornamental purposes due to their aesthetic foliage.
 
 
 
• **Evolutionary Importance:**
 
 
• Pteridophytes bridge the evolutionary gap between non-vascular bryophytes and seed-bearing gymnosperms.
 
• They exhibit structural adaptations such as true roots, stems, and leaves, reflecting significant evolutionary progress.
 
• Unlike bryophytes, they reproduce via spores and do not depend on water for fertilization.

questions.question: In July 2023, the District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) in Tirupathur district, Tamil Nadu, achieved a monumental achievement by constructing 1546 farm ponds in just 30 days, setting a new world record. This remarkable initiative was carried out under which government scheme?

options.text: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In July 2023, the District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) of Tirupathur district, Tamil Nadu, constructed **1546 farm ponds in just 30 days**, setting a new world record.
 
• This initiative was carried out under the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS)**, a flagship government program.
 
• MGNREGS aims to provide guaranteed wage employment to rural households and promote sustainable rural development projects such as **water conservation and management.**
 
• The construction of farm ponds under this scheme **enhances water availability** for agriculture and helps mitigate the adverse effects of drought.
 
• This achievement reflects the dual objective of MGNREGS to **generate rural employment and create durable assets** that improve infrastructure and resilience to climate change.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS)**

 
 
• Launched in 2005, it is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India.
 
• It provides a legal guarantee of **100 days of wage employment** per financial year to every rural household.
 
• The scheme primarily focuses on **labor-intensive works** such as water conservation, drought-proofing, irrigation, and land development.
 
• MGNREGS is a demand-driven program, meaning work is provided based on the needs of rural households.
 
 
 
• **Farm Ponds**
 
 
• Farm ponds are small water storage structures built to collect and store surface runoff or rainwater.
 
• They play a crucial role in **addressing water scarcity** and ensuring year-round irrigation for agriculture.
 
• Farm ponds help in **groundwater recharge**, reduce soil erosion, and support sustainable farming practices.
 
• They are particularly beneficial in **drought-prone regions** to combat climate variability.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) Alignment**
 
 
• MGNREGS supports SDG 1 (**No Poverty**) through rural employment generation.
 
• Farm ponds contribute to SDG 6 (**Clean Water and Sanitation**) by enhancing water availability for agriculture.
 
• The scheme also aligns with SDG 13 (**Climate Action**) by improving resilience against climate change.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Water Conservation**
 
 
• Water conservation is essential for ensuring agricultural productivity, especially in rain-fed regions.
 
• Efficient water management practices, such as farm ponds, help in **mitigating climate change** impacts and ensuring food security.
 
• Such initiatives contribute to maintaining ecological balance and preventing resource depletion in rural areas.

questions.question: By which of the following Amendments was the right to property removed from Part III of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**44th Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **44th Amendment Act** of the Indian Constitution, enacted in **1978**, removed the right to property from the category of Fundamental Rights under Part III of the Constitution.
 
• After the amendment, the right to property was reclassified as a **legal right** under Article 300A in Part XII of the Constitution.
 
• This change was made during the tenure of the **Janata Party government**, led by Prime Minister **Morarji Desai**.
 
• The primary objective of this amendment was to facilitate **land reforms** and prevent misuse of the right to property by affluent individuals to challenge government policies.
 
• Post-amendment, property disputes are dealt with as violations of legal rights rather than Fundamental Rights, ensuring streamlined governance and justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights in Part III**

 
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Articles 12 to 35 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These rights are essential for safeguarding individual freedoms and are enforceable by the courts.
 
• Major Fundamental Rights include the Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.
 
 
 
• **Legal Rights vs Fundamental Rights**
 
 
• Fundamental Rights are protected by the Constitution and cannot be altered without constitutional amendment.
 
• Legal rights are granted by ordinary legislation and can be modified or revoked by the legislature.
 
• The 44th Amendment reclassified the right to property as a legal right under Article 300A.
 
 
 
• **Article 300A of the Constitution**
 
 
• Article 300A states: "No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law."
 
• This provision ensures that property can only be taken by the government through legally established procedures.
 
 
 
• **Land Reforms in India**
 
 
• Land reforms aim to redistribute land ownership and increase agricultural productivity.
 
• The removal of the right to property as a Fundamental Right facilitated initiatives like the abolition of the zamindari system and ceilings on landholding.

questions.question: Divergent plate boundary is a boundary that occurs between two tectonic plates:

options.text: that are moving towards one another
where one plate slides beneath the other
that are sliding horizontally past each other
that are moving away from one another

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Divergent plate boundary is a boundary that occurs between two tectonic plates that are moving away from one another.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Divergent plate boundaries occur where two tectonic plates move away from each other, creating a gap.
 
• These boundaries are often associated with the formation of new oceanic crust as magma rises from the mantle to fill the gap.
 
• Shallow earthquakes and volcanic activity are common phenomena observed at divergent boundaries.
 
• Examples of divergent boundaries include mid-ocean ridges like the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
 
• The process of seafloor spreading is a hallmark of divergent plate boundaries, contributing to the gradual expansion of ocean basins.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tectonic Plate Boundaries**

 
 
• The Earth's lithosphere is divided into tectonic plates that move relative to each other.
 
• There are three main types of plate boundaries: divergent (moving apart), convergent (moving together), and transform (sliding past one another).
 
• These boundaries are responsible for geological phenomena such as earthquakes, volcanic activity, and mountain formation.
 
 
 
• **Seafloor Spreading**
 
 
• Occurs at divergent plate boundaries where magma rises and solidifies to create new crust.
 
• Magnetic anomalies on the ocean floor provide evidence for this process, showing symmetrical patterns on either side of mid-ocean ridges.
 
 
 
• **Mid-Ocean Ridges**
 
 
• Underwater mountain ranges formed by divergent plate boundaries.
 
• Known for high volcanic activity and the generation of new crust.
 
• Examples include the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and the East Pacific Rise.
 
 
 
• **Rift Zones**
 
 
• Occur when divergent boundaries form within continental plates, creating rift valleys.
 
• Over time, these rift zones can evolve into ocean basins.
 
• The East African Rift is a prominent example of an active rift zone.

questions.question: Who discovered the Bharhut stupa?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alexander Cunningham**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Alexander Cunningham**, regarded as the "Father of Indian Archaeology," discovered the Bharhut Stupa in **1873**.
 
• He extensively documented the stupa's remains, including its intricate sculptures and inscriptions, which are valuable for understanding early Buddhist art and architecture.
 
• The Bharhut Stupa, located in present-day **Madhya Pradesh**, dates back to the **2nd century BCE**, showcasing early Buddhist relief carvings and inscriptions in the Brahmi script.
 
• Cunningham's discovery provided critical insights into the cultural and religious practices of the **Mauryan and Sunga periods**.
 
• His findings on Bharhut are recorded in his archaeological reports, which remain foundational for the study of ancient Indian history and early Buddhist art.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharhut Stupa**

 
 
• The Bharhut Stupa is an ancient Buddhist monument known for its remarkable railings and gateways adorned with narrative relief sculptures.
 
• Its carvings depict **Jataka tales** (stories of the Buddha’s previous lives) and other Buddhist symbols.
 
• It was originally commissioned during the **Mauryan Empire** and later renovated during the **Sunga dynasty**.
 
• Many artifacts from Bharhut, including reliefs and inscriptions, are now preserved in the **Indian Museum in Kolkata**.
 
 
 
• **Alexander Cunningham**
 
 
• Alexander Cunningham was the first **Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**, founded in 1861.
 
• He conducted pioneering archaeological explorations of major sites like **Sarnath, Taxila, and Bodh Gaya**.
 
• His systematic documentation and study of inscriptions helped reconstruct India’s ancient history and timeline.
 
• Cunningham's work laid the foundation for modern archaeology in India.
 
 
 
• **Buddhist Art and Architecture**
 
 
• The Bharhut Stupa is an example of **early Buddhist art**, characterized by narrative reliefs and symbolic depictions of Buddhist themes.
 
• Unlike later Buddhist monuments, early art like Bharhut avoided anthropomorphic representations of the Buddha, instead using symbols like the **lotus and wheel**.
 
• The railings and gateways of Bharhut illustrate the transition to more elaborate decorative elements seen in later sites like **Sanchi**.
 
• Inscriptions at Bharhut provide valuable evidence of early Buddhist practices, patronage, and the use of the **Brahmi script**.
 
 
 
• **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**
 
 
• The ASI, established in 1861, is responsible for preserving and documenting India’s cultural heritage.
 
• It conducts excavations, research, and conservation of historical monuments and archaeological sites.
 
• Under Cunningham’s leadership, the ASI began systematic archaeological surveys and excavations in India.
 
• The efforts of the ASI have been instrumental in understanding India’s ancient civilization and its contributions to global heritage.
